facts.hook: Rebuilding Khufu's funeral boat took fourteen years
facts.body: It was found in 1954 buried in a pit beside the Great Pyramid. The ship was reassembled piece by piece over fourteen years.

facts.hook: The Great Pyramid's sarcophagus went in before the pyramid was finished
facts.body: The granite sarcophagus in the King's Chamber is too big to turn the corner between the passages, so it must have been set in place before the chamber's roof.

facts.hook: The Rosetta Stone looked black because of the wax that protected it
facts.body: In London it was covered in carnauba wax to protect it from visitors' fingers. The wax darkened the stone and it was mistaken for black basalt; a 1999 cleaning revealed its original dark grey.

facts.hook: The Rosetta Stone spent two years 15 metres underground in a postal railway station
facts.body: Towards the end of the First World War, in 1917, the museum moved it to safety from the bombing of London, to a station of the Postal Tube Railway.

facts.hook: An Egyptian decree called hieroglyphs the "language of the gods"
facts.body: The decree ordered a copy in every temple in three scripts: hieroglyphs, Demotic, and Greek, the language used by the Ptolemaic government.

facts.hook: Tutankhamun was one of the few pharaohs worshipped as a god while alive
facts.body: Temples for his cult were built as far away as Nubia, including one at Kawa and a smaller one at Faras.

facts.hook: Tutankhamun was first named "living image of Aten"
facts.body: He was born Tutankhaten, after the god Aten of his father Akhenaten. When traditional worship was restored, Aten gave way to Amun in his name.

facts.hook: According to Lucian, Sostratus hid his name under plaster on Alexandria's lighthouse
facts.body: In the second century AD, Lucian wrote that Sostratus hid his name under plaster bearing Ptolemy's name, so it would show in the stone once the plaster fell off.

facts.hook: Alexandria's harbour hid 30 sphinxes and 5 obelisks beside the lighthouse ruins
facts.body: In 1994 French archaeologists found remains of the lighthouse in the Eastern Harbour, including granite blocks of 49 to 60 tonnes.

facts.hook: Spanish, French and Italian words for lighthouse come from the island of Pharos
facts.body: The Alexandria lighthouse stood on the island of Pharos. Its name came to mean "lighthouse" in Greek and was borrowed by Romance languages such as Spanish, French and Italian.

facts.hook: The platypus hunts with its eyes, ears and nose shut
facts.body: Underwater it closes its eyes, ears and nose and digs along the stream bed with its bill. Electroreceptors in the bill detect the tiny electric currents made when its prey's muscles contract.

facts.hook: A hummingbird can slow its metabolism to 1/15 of normal
facts.body: When food is scarce or at night, hummingbirds enter torpor, a state like hibernation, and slow their metabolic rate to one fifteenth of its normal rate.

facts.hook: Hummingbird eggs are the smallest of any bird
facts.body: A hummingbird typically lays two pea-sized white eggs, which are incubated for two to three weeks.

facts.hook: Some male hummingbirds court by diving from 30 metres
facts.body: During courtship some species dive from 30 metres above a female at around 23 m/s, which is about 83 km/h.

facts.hook: Chameleons change colour more to show their state than to hide
facts.body: Colour change can help with camouflage, but it is used most commonly for social signalling and in reaction to temperature. It tells other chameleons about the animal's physical condition and intentions.

facts.hook: Chameleons move each eye on its own
facts.body: Each eye can pivot and focus independently, so a chameleon can watch two objects at once. When it hunts, the eyes focus forward together.
